e: Unadapted borrowing from Welsh cwm (“valley”). Doublet of combe.
q: A fine glacier descends from Mount Longstaff. It has cut very deep and the walls stand at an angle of at least 50°. Otherwise, although there are many cwms on the lower ranges, the mountains themselves seem little carved.
1913, Robert Falcon Scott, Scott's Last Expedition, Volume 1, Chapter 16:
Cantref Penwedig, subdivided into the cwmwds of Geneu'r Glyn, Perfedd, and Creuddyn[…]
1822, Memoirs of Owen Glendower (Owain Glyndwr), page xiii:
It is situated in a cwmwd which still retains the name of Swydd-y-Grè, i. e., the office or jurisdiction of the Grè.
